title: Protecting persons outside the lawsuit
summary: A judgment ordinarily does not bind a person who was neither a party nor represented through a recognized exception. Yet litigation can still practically impair an absentee’s interests even without formally binding that person.
notes: Knowledge of litigation is not itself a universal substitute for party status or adequate representation. Do not convert a reserved issue about possible intervention consequences into an automatic rule.

sections.Meaning: A judgment ordinarily does not bind a person who was neither a party nor represented through a recognized exception. Yet litigation can still practically impair an absentee’s interests even without formally binding that person.
sections.How to work through the question: Identify the property, fund, or right at risk; distinguish formal preclusion from practical harm; and consider joinder, intervention, representation, or tailored relief. Provident and Hansberry address different protections for absent persons.
